147983.overview: Roller Coaster is a portable electronic game released by VTech under the Time & Fun brand in 1984. Apparently, this device was created in the likeness of the then popular series of portable electronic games Game & Watch from Nintendo.

162016.overview: The player must help the character move the clotheslines from getting his hanged clothes wet. When the player reaches 100 points, it stops raining for a brief moment before raining again, and the player receives 10 points. As the player progresses in the game, the raindrops will fall faster. If a raindrop hits a shirt, the boy will angrily wring it out and the player will get a miss. If the player gets 300 points without any misses, the points will be worth double until the player does get a miss. If the player has any misses at said score, all misses will be removed instead. On hard mode, a crow will appear and move the clotheslines, similar to Waluigi's role in Modern Mode. When the player gets three misses, they receive a Game Over.

190418.overview: Robocop 2 is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie Robocop 2 from 1990.

190419.overview: Robocop 3 is a handheld LCD electronic video game developed by Tiger Electronics, based on the movie Robocop 3 from 1993.

194496.overview:
This handheld version of Battle Arena Toshinden adapts Takara’s console fighting series into Tiger Electronics’ R-Zone format. The player chooses a warrior armed with bladed weapons and competes in one-on-one duels against successive opponents, aiming to claim the title of champion in the mysterious Toshinden tournament.

The R-Zone platform projects the game’s monochrome visuals onto a mirrored eyepiece. Each R-Zone cartridge contains its own transparent LCD panel; when inserted, red light from the console illuminates the panel, and the image appears as a floating display before the player’s eye. Controls consist of a small D-pad and buttons wired to the main unit.

Within these constraints, Battle Arena Toshinden presents a simplified interpretation of its 3-D source. Directional inputs move the fighter left and right, while the attack button triggers weapon strikes. Each round measures success by a segmented health bar at the top of the image. Winning a bout advances to a faster and more aggressive rival. Gameplay alternates between timing defensive parries and launching attacks when an opening appears, the LCD’s limited animation conveying the rhythm of combat through flashing silhouettes and sound cues.

194497.overview:
R-Zone: Batman Forever places the player in control of Batman navigating urban environments to stop villains from executing their schemes. The mission includes chasing, dodging enemy traps, and defeating foes within the limitations of the R-Zone’s LCD mirror projection system.

The R-Zone’s cartridge contains a transparent LCD panel that gets reflected via a mirror to the player’s eye. Using direction controls, Batman moves through layered screen zones, avoiding hazards and enemies. The player triggers attacks or gadgets via action inputs when enemies appear in reach. As levels progress, enemy patterns intensify, requiring sharper reflexes and anticipation. The system displays animated segments of Batman, enemies, projectiles, and damage indicators by activating or shading pre-drawn LCD cells.

Some rounds end with mini-boss or theme-relevant encounters, and timing is essential to avoid overlapping attacks from multiple directions. Lives are limited, and failing them forces a restart.

194498.overview:
Indy 500 for the Tiger R-Zone is a vastly simplified, officially licensed LCD racing game developed by Tiger Electronics and released in 1995. Though it shares its branding and artwork with Sega's famous 1995 arcade racer, the gameplay is fundamentally adapted to match the strict hardware limitations of the notorious R-Zone console.

True to Tiger's classic formula, the gameplay is simple, arcade-style, and highly repetitive. Players navigate a single-lane track, shifting gears and steering to dodge oncoming pixelated rival cars before time runs out.

478647.overview: In Road Runner, the player takes control of the Road Runner. The Road Runner must run along the road, avoiding trucks, landmines, falling rocks, etc. and also not get caught by Wile E. Coyote. The Road Runner must also eat birdseed along the way or he will become faint and Wile E. will catch him.

479773.overview:
Play as your favorite Rugrat - Phil, Lil, Chuckie, or Tommy!
Explore the carnival and collect as many Reptar treats as you can.
